2. The case of the plaintiffs filed in Title Suit No. 213 of 1972 in the Court of Munsif (now joint Assistant Judge), Bagerhat, in short, is that his predecessor and the predecessor of the defendant No. 1 were the original owners of the suit land. The superior landlords, Biseswar Saha and others auction purchased the suit land and got delivery possession through Court. By amicable arrangement Biseswar Saha alone got the suit land. Thereafter, he settled the same with the plaintiffs' predecessors orally in Baishakh, 1357 B.S. Subsequently, the defendant No. 6 granted a patta in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessors recognizing the oral settlement on 18.05.1953. Since then the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land. 1. 

 9. The plaintiffs' case is that the entire suit land was sold in auction and landlords Biseswar Saha and others auction purchased the suit land and got delivery of possession through Court. By amicable arrangement Biseswar Saha got the entire suit land and thereafter, orally settled the suit land to the plaintiffs' predecessors in Baishakh, 1357 B.S. and subsequently defendant No.6 granted a patta in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessors on 18.05.1953 .recognizing the oral settlement. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. After Baishakh, 1372 B.S. the defendant No. 1 approached the father of the plaintiff No. 11 for permission to reside in some portion of the suit land temporarily and permission was granted but subsequently plaintiffs asked the defendant Nos. 1- 4 to vacate the suit land but the defendants did not vacate and finally refused in ASHWIN, 1379 B.S Hence the suit. 

 10. The defendant No. 1 case, on the other hand, is that the superior landlords never auction the purchased land and landlord never got delivery of possession of the suit land and never settled the same orally with plaintiffs' predecessors and the patta in favour of the plaintiff is a collusive and created one. 

 14. The trial court and the appellate Court also held that the defendant No.1 took settlement of the suit land as vested property. If he had interest in the suit land as claimed by him, he ought to have taken steps to get the- suit land released from the list of Enemy (now vested) property but in this case the defendant No. 1 without doing so took settlement of the suit land from the vested property authority as vested and nonresident property. This conduct of the defendant No.1 definitely proves that he has no title and possession in the suit land and this also supports the case of the plaintiffs. The patta Ext A granted by landlord Biseswar Saha in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessors recognizing the oral settlement on 18.05.1953 after auction purchase' has been filed by the plaintiffs. The Exts.1 and 7 clearly go to show that the plaintiffs have acquired title in the suit land and they also have possession in the suit land.
